newsitem.title: USA: Nutrition may help fight tuberculosis - study.
newsitem.headline: Nutrition may help fight tuberculosis - study.

text.p: Proper nutrition might be an important weapon against tuberculosis, which has re-emerged as a major public health threat around the world in the past few years, researchers said on Monday.
An estimated 3 million to 4 million people a year die of tuberculosis. Some strains of the disease that resist standard medications have also appeared.

In an experiment on mice exposed to TB, researchers at Albert Einstein College of Medicine in New York found that the animals given a low-protein diet were more likely to become ill than those given a high-protein diet.

Moreover, those who got sick had a better chance of survival when their diet was switched to high protein. The study by Dr. Barry Bloom and colleagues will appear on Tuesday in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

Although more work would have to be done to see if the same thing happens in people, Bloom wrote that the research may lead to "new and inexpensive nutritional or therapeutic strategies that will enable malnourished hosts (of the TB germ) to be protected against tuberculosis and other infectious diseases."

The protein-deprived mice showed lower levels of three molecules that have a role in killing bacteria. But these effects were not permanent and the levels went back to normal once the protein was added to the diet.

In a related commentary in the journal, Ranjit Kumar Chandra of Memorial University of Newfoundland in Canada said that the "seminal" work by Bloom's team could help lead to inexpensive nutritional strategies for fighting TB.

"The era of nutritional manipulation of the immune system has finally dawned and it brings with it the promise of using diet and nutrition as innovative powerful tools to reduce illness and death caused by infection," he wrote.
